external_collaboration.evidence_quote: TEAMing-up with families is the heart of what we do. We provide therapy for children at our clinics, in homes, at preschools, elementary schools, and throughout our community. We also serve internationally through the TEAMworks Non-Profit in Belize, Guatemala, Rwanda, China and Ukraine. Locally, we serve families in Fayetteville, Bentonville, Rogers, Prairie Grove, Winslow, Siloam Springs, Elkins, Farmington, Greenland, Lowell, Pea Ridge, and surrounding areas.

Sherrie’s work with children who have special needs initially began during her studies at Cal State in Monterey Bay, California. There, she minored in human movement and adapted physical education. After graduating in 2009, Sherrie’s passion for children laid the groundwork for her future career in pediatrics.

Sydney Kinser holds a Doctor of Physical Therapy degree from Arkansas State University. She earned her Bachelor of Science in exercise science with a minor in pre-professional healthcare studies from Harding University.

Sydney is actively involved with Bentonville Church of Christ. When not working, she enjoys going on walks, shopping, and trying new coffee shops and restaurants with her husband.

Daryn brings a diverse background of experience to her role at The Grace School. She worked with the University of Arkansas EMPOWER Program for four years. There, she provided one-on-one support to college students with developmental and cognitive disabilities. Additionally, her experience as a Pediatric Patient Liaison at Ozark Prosthodontics have equipped her with a deep understanding of family-centered care. She also values the importance of implementing structured, positive routines.

David Gomez, M.S., BCBA, holds a Master of Science in psychology with an emphasis in ABA from Walden University and a Bachelor of Arts in psychology from California State University Long Beach. He served as a TEAM ABA Fellow prior to earning his BCBA credential. He draws on ABA treatment experience in home-health, school-based, and clinic-based settings. He shares, “It is an honor and a privilege to be part of guiding students’ growth towards independence.”
